setup: Buffalo (9–1) hosts Kansas City (8–2) in a Thanksgiving meeting of two AFC contenders. The Bills just beat Miami 26–9 while the Chiefs defeated Arizona 34–7. Josh Allen and Patrick Mahomes renew a rivalry in which Buffalo has enjoyed regular-season success but Kansas City has won all four playoff meetings between the quarterbacks.

things.title: Kansas City's explosive run game
things.body: The Chiefs rank second in yards per rush and explosive runs. Buffalo must prevent the ground game from creating favorable passing downs for Mahomes, whose offense can exploit defenders drawn toward the line.

things.title: Finishing in the red zone
things.body: Buffalo has scored on all 41 red-zone trips this season, but six of its last 12 scoring drives inside the 20 ended in field goals. Against Kansas City's offense, turning those opportunities into touchdowns matters.

things.title: Allen against a stronger test
things.body: Buffalo's recent winning stretch included several opponents starting backup quarterbacks. Against Mahomes, Allen and the offense need sustained drives and sound decisions to keep the Chiefs from controlling possession.

breakdown.bottom_line: Buffalo's home field and strong record meet a Kansas City team with an explosive rushing attack and a proven quarterback. The red-zone battle, explosive plays and possession efficiency will shape this AFC showdown.
